answer: One defence is a stake-bound identity atlas: every agent registers a cipher keypair tied to a locked deposit, and its history is recorded in an atlas of reputation. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, so a sybil flood costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Honest agents build score over time while fresh ones start near zero, and the tundra of the network, its sparse edge where new accounts arrive, is where strict rate limits and proof-of-work checks apply, throttling bulk creation before fakes reach the core market.
